question: Should OpenClaw adopt ordered, first-declaration-owned configuration layers with narrowly defined monotonic tool-policy exceptions as a supported core contract?
rationale: The RFC creates a new CLI and configuration surface that may reject existing overlay patterns and runtime writes; tests prove behavior but cannot decide long-term product compatibility or security policy.

options.title: Accept the V1 contract
options.body: Approve the startup-only immutable model and coordinate RFC acceptance with the linked implementation after upgrade and security review.

options.title: Revise authority semantics
options.body: Keep the RFC in draft while narrowing path ownership, monotonic exceptions, or runtime-write behavior.

options.title: Decline core layering
options.body: Keep composition in host-specific tooling rather than establishing this contract in OpenClaw core.

recommendation.title: Accept the V1 contract
recommendation.body: Approve the startup-only immutable model and coordinate RFC acceptance with the linked implementation after upgrade and security review.

likelyOwner.reason: The timeline shows direct involvement in the design discussion and this person is the strongest available routing candidate for the core product choice.
